newsitem.title: UK: WEEK AHEAD - Markets focus on interest rate picture.
newsitem.headline: WEEK AHEAD - Markets focus on interest rate picture.

text.p: Financial markets will look for further indications of a possible interest rate rise in the United States and rate cuts in Italy and Spain in the week ahead, economists said on Friday.
"In the U.S. we have reasonably important statistics coming out, with industrial production most prominent," said Simon Knapp, international economist at Barclays de Zoete Wedd here.
"The question is how quickly is the Fed going to raise rates, and how much by," he added.
March industrial production data are due on Wednesday.

The figures come hard on the heels of retail sales and producer price (PPI) data on Friday, which knocked U.S. Treasuries and fuelled speculation of a U.S. rate hike at the next Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting in May.

If strong industrial production figures follow Friday's high upward revision in February retail sales, economists will raise their forecasts for gross domestic product (GDP) for the first quarter, to be released on April 30, Knapp said.
U.S. industrial production rose by 0.5 percent in February.
In addition, U.S. March consumer prices (CPI) will be released on Tuesday.
"Markets will be worried that the underlying core (excluding food and energy) CPI rate will pick up," said Ian Harwood, head of strategy and economics at Kleinwort Benson in London.
Core consumer prices came in at 0.2 percent in February.
Market participants concerned about the heady rise of the dollar will be watching U.S. trade data for February, to be released on Thursday, economists said.
Also on Thursday, the Philadelphia Fed index for April will provide some of the earliest information about economic activity in that month, they added.
Economists are pencilling in Friday as the first day for the possible release of CPI data from the Italian cities.
"We are building up for a 50-75 basis point cut in Italian interest rates if these figures are good," said John Shepperd, chief economist at Yamaichi International in London.
"But politics are a constraint, with the government under pressure," he added.
Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi survived a first confidence vote in the Italian upper house on Thursday over the proposed sending of a security force to Albania.
The Italian lower house began its confidence debate on Friday and was scheduled to vote on Saturday.
There is little major Spanish data due, but the past week's benign inflation data allow for monetary easing, economists said.
"There could be a modest cut in interest rates at the end of next week, or one or two weeks away," said Shepperd.
In Germany, the Bundesbank holds its fortnightly council meeting on Thursday, but no interest rate change is expected.
In Britain, inflation will be a focus, with the release of March PPI on Monday, February average earnings on Wednesday, and March retail prices on Thursday.
Emerging markets will be watching the annual meeting of the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD).
